Personal finance guide

EMI Planning Guide India

Learn how EMI, tenure, interest rate, and prepayment affect the real cost of a loan.

EMI comfort can hide total cost

A lower EMI usually comes from a longer tenure. That can help monthly cash flow, but the total interest paid over the loan can rise sharply.

Before accepting a loan offer, compare EMI, total interest, total repayment, and how much of your monthly income remains for savings and emergencies.

Interest rate changes matter most on large loans

A small rate difference can create a large total-cost difference on home loans or long-tenure education loans. Always compare lender offers using the same amount and tenure.

Floating-rate loans should be tested with a higher-rate scenario so you know whether the EMI remains manageable.

Prepayment is strongest early

In a reducing-balance loan, early EMIs contain a larger interest component. Prepaying in the early years can reduce the principal faster and save more interest.

Check the lender's prepayment and foreclosure rules before assuming every extra payment will be free.

Action checklist

  • - Compare total repayment, not only EMI.
  • - Keep total EMIs within a comfortable income range.
  • - Check processing, insurance, and foreclosure charges.
  • - Test a higher interest-rate scenario.
  • - Use bonuses for prepayment only after emergency savings are ready.
